design:
D1 No guessing a database. `hub/hub/config.py` makes `database_url` a required setting whose default factory raises `HubNotToldWhichDatabase`; the CLI is what computes the default path and passes it, so only a launcher that chose a database reaches one.

D2 Profiles are separate data directories and PID files; named profiles require `--port`, and `reset` takes exactly one profile.

D3 The app window is `pywebview` when available, else a chromeless browser; the detached Hub is independent of the window.

D4 Shutdown order (`hub/hub/main.py` lifespan): stop scheduler, terminate run processes, settle background run tasks (max 5 passes), then `engine.dispose()`. A `checkout` listener in `hub/hub/db/engine.py` invalidates connections whose aiosqlite worker thread is dead, and they are closed without waiting on that thread.
lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: An operator with a real instance and trial instances on one machine must never have a launch silently attach to the wrong database, and a stopping instance must neither hang nor strand work.

requirements.rationale: One entry point means one path to test and one thing to tell a new operator.
requirements.statement: Running `agentweave` with no subcommand SHALL launch or reuse the local instance, open or register the invocation directory as a project through it, and open the app at that project; the CLI SHALL offer no other way to begin (no `init`, `activate`, `quick` or `start`).

requirements.rationale: Only the project should vary with the launch directory, never the instance; an explicit `DATABASE_URL` is the operator's instruction.
requirements.statement: Bare `agentweave` (native, `--docker` or `--local`) and `docker compose up` against the Hub's compose file SHALL resolve to the same database for a given profile whatever directory they are run from, and a `DATABASE_URL` already in the environment SHALL be passed through unchanged.

requirements.rationale: The default path is where the operator's real work lives; a process reaching it by accident would migrate and write it exactly as one that meant to.
requirements.statement: A Hub process started without `DATABASE_URL` in its environment or in a `.env` in its working directory (direct `uvicorn hub.main:app`, `agentweave-hub`) MUST refuse to start before opening, creating or migrating any database, naming the default path it declined and both ways to choose one.

requirements.rationale: An unintended attachment should be readable at the moment it happens.
requirements.statement: A Hub told which database to open SHALL log, at a level its default logging shows and before it first opens the file, the absolute path it resolved and whether the file already existed; a relative path it was given SHALL be resolved against its working directory as written.

requirements.rationale: The operator manages one instance per profile, not per project.
requirements.statement: `agentweave status` SHALL report whether the instance is running, its URL and runtime, how many projects are registered and which was opened most recently; `agentweave stop` SHALL stop that one instance.

requirements.rationale: Reset is irreversible; its blast radius must be exactly one profile and never the operator's code.
requirements.statement: `agentweave reset` SHALL delete Hub state only after the operator types `yes`, SHALL target only the default profile's data or only the one named with `--profile`, and MUST NOT delete any registered project directory or source.

requirements.rationale: The Hub owns execution; a second writer of collaboration state is a second runtime.
requirements.statement: The CLI SHALL provide no command that sends a message, creates or updates a task, asks or answers a question, manages agents, or manages jobs; those SHALL be reachable only through the app (operator) or the agent capability plane (agents).

requirements.rationale: App mode is the default for every normal launch, so it should look like an app, not a browser tab.
requirements.statement: Every app-mode launch, native or Docker, SHALL open the app in a dedicated chromeless desktop window titled AgentWeave when `pywebview` is installed and can create one, and the invoking command SHALL stay running until that window is closed.

requirements.rationale: The webview is an optional extra; its absence must never block reaching the app.
requirements.statement: When no webview backend is installed or it fails to create a window, the launch SHALL report what failed and fall back to a chromeless browser window or the default browser without crashing, and SHALL return without waiting for that window.

requirements.rationale: Agents keep working when the operator closes the window.
requirements.statement: Closing the app window MUST NOT stop the detached Hub process.

requirements.rationale: A native webview needs the main thread, which a foreground server already occupies.
requirements.statement: A `--no-detach` start SHALL use the browser behaviour even when a webview is installed, keeping the server in the foreground until interrupted.

requirements.rationale: A deleted shortcut is a decision; one that reappears every start is worse than none.
requirements.statement: On Windows, a launch SHALL offer to create an `AgentWeave.lnk` Desktop shortcut once per install, recorded by a marker whether or not creation succeeded, SHALL never overwrite an existing shortcut, and `--desktop-shortcut` SHALL ask again.

requirements.rationale: Trial instances must be unable to touch the real one by construction.
requirements.statement: `agentweave`, `status`, `stop`, `doctor` and `reset` SHALL accept `--profile <name>` (default `default`); a named profile SHALL resolve to its own database beneath `~/.agentweave/hub/profiles/<name>/` and its own PID file, the default profile SHALL keep its existing path, and an explicit `DATABASE_URL` SHALL override either.

requirements.rationale: The default port is where the default profile normally runs.
requirements.statement: A `--profile` other than `default` without `--port` SHALL exit with an error naming both flags and SHALL NOT start or address the default port.

requirements.rationale: Releasing connections first strands runs that still need them; settling before the scheduler stops settles a set that can refill. An instance asked to stop must stop.
requirements.statement: On shutdown the instance SHALL, while its event loop still runs, stop admitting scheduled work, then settle the background run tasks it started (including successors they schedule, up to a bounded number of passes, logging any left), and only then release every database connection.

requirements.rationale: Such a connection accepts work, never answers, and cannot be closed; anything that waits on it waits forever.
requirements.statement: The instance SHALL NOT hand out a pooled SQLite connection whose driver worker thread has ended, SHALL transparently replace it with a new connection, and SHALL NOT wait on such a connection when closing it on any path, including shutdown and abandoned checkouts.

requirements.rationale: The documented form once reported a running Hub as stopped with no error.
requirements.statement: `--port` and `--profile` given before the subcommand SHALL take effect for `status`, `stop`, `doctor` and `reset`; given in both places, the value nearer the subcommand SHALL win; no accepted option MAY be silently ignored.

in_scope: `status`, `stop`, `reset`, and where `--port` and `--profile` may be given relative to a subcommand
Database selection and the refusal to guess

Shutdown ordering and dead database connections
non_goals: What `doctor` checks, including environment readiness: runtime-diagnostics

summary: The one supported way to start and manage a local AgentWeave instance: bare `agentweave` launches or reuses the instance, registers the invocation directory as a project and opens the app; `status`, `stop` and `reset` manage it, honouring global options wherever the documented command form places them; named profiles give separate instances; the Hub refuses to guess which database to open; and shutdown releases what it holds in a safe order.
